description: Put a keyframe on an interpolable at a given time, or overwrite the one already there. The intended workflow is to omit 'value': the keyframe then captures the property exactly as the scene stands, which is what Timeline's own button does — pose the character with studio_set_character_bone / studio_set_character_ik / studio_set_object_transform, seek to the time you want, and record. Pass 'value' only to set it directly, in the same shape studio_timeline_get_state reads it back: a number, a boolean, [x,y,z] for a position or scale, euler degrees for a rotation, [r,g,b,a] for a colour. Requires the Timeline plugin.

time.description: seconds, between 0 and the timeline duration; an existing keyframe at the same time is overwritten

value.description: omit to capture the current scene value — the reliable option, and the only one for types with no JSON form

curve.description: easing from this keyframe to the next: one of Timeline's own presets ('line' linear, 'top' fast then slow, 'bottom' slow then fast, 'hermite' eased both ends, 'stairs' a hard step), or explicit [time, value, in_tangent, out_tangent] points where a null tangent means an infinite one. Omitted, it inherits the curve of the preceding keyframe and falls back to linear.

output.description: the interpolable with all its keyframes, same shape as one entry of studio_timeline_get_state's 'interpolables'
